questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of $150ms^{- 1}$. The ratio of velocity after $3s$~and $5s$ is~$\dfrac{x + 1}{x}$.~The value of $x$ is _____.~{take, g = 10ms^{- 2}}
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the velocity of the ball after& $3s$~is given by

${v}_{3} = u - 3g . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the velocity of the ball after~$5s$~is given by

${v}_{5} = u - 5g . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (1) by equation (2) to obtain the required ratio.

$\dfrac{v3}{v5} = \dfrac{u - 3g}{u - 5g} . . . \left(3\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required ratio.

\begin{cases}\dfrac{v3}{v5}$& = & $\dfrac{150 - 30}{150 - 50}$\\ & = & $\dfrac{120}{100}$\\ & = & $\dfrac{6}{5}$\\ & = & $\dfrac{5 + 1}{5}\end{cases}

Comparing the above equation with the given expression, it can be written that~$x = 5.

$

questions.q:
A NCC parade is going at a uniform speed of $9kmh^{- 1}$ under a mango tree on which a monkey is sitting at a height of $19 . 6m$. At any particular instant, the monkey drops a mango. A cadet will receive the mango whose distance from the tree at time of drop is :
(Given $g = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If a cadet receives the mango, then the time taken by the mango to fall and the cadet to reach there should be equal.

Time taken by mango to fall& $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$.

$⇒ t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 19 . 6}{9 . 8}} = 2s$

Therefore, the distance of the cadet from the tree will be,~$d = vt$.

$⇒ d = 9 \times \dfrac{5}{18} \times 2 = 5m$

questions.q: A car accelerates from rest at a constant rate $\alpha$ for some time after which it decelerates at a constant rate $\beta$ to come to rest. If the total time elapsed is t seconds, the total distance travelled is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${v}_{0} = \alpha{t}_{1}$~and~$0 = {v}_{0} - \beta{t}_{2} ⇒ {v}_{0} = \beta{t}_{2}$

${t}_{1} + {t}_{2} = t$

${v}_{0}\left(\dfrac{1}{α} + \dfrac{1}{β}\right) = t$

$⇒ {v}_{0} = \dfrac{\alpha\betat}{\alpha + \beta}$

Distance $=$ area of $v - t$~graph

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times t \times {v}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times t \times \dfrac{\alpha\betat}{\alpha + \beta} = \dfrac{\alpha\betat^{2}}{2 ( \alpha + \beta )}$

questions.q: The position of a particle as a function of time $t,$ is given by $x\left(t\right) = at + bt^{2} - ct^{3}$ where $a, b$ and $c$ are constants. When the particles zero acceleration, then its velocity will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$x ( t ) = at + bt^{2} - ct^{3}$
velocity $v ( t ) = \dfrac{d}{dt} ( x ) = \dfrac{d}{dt} \left(at + bt^{2} - ct^{3}\right)$
$= a + 2bt - 3ct^{2}$
Acceleration $= $\dfrac{d}{dt}$v ( t ) = 2b - 6tc$
$\text{acceleration} =0 ⇒ 2b - 6tc = 0$
$t = $\dfrac{b}{3c}
$∴$ velocity when $t = $\dfrac{b}{3c},
v \left($t = \dfrac{b}{3c}\right) =a + $2b\left(\dfrac{b}{3c}\right) --3\$left(\dfrac{b}{3c}\right)$2$
$= a + $\dfrac{2b^{2}}{3c} - \dfrac{b^{2}}{3c}
$= a + \dfrac{b^{2}}{3c}$

questions.q: Train A is moving along two parallel rail tracks towards north with $72kmh^{- 1}$ and train $B$ is moving towards south with speed $108kmh^{- 1}$. Velocity of train $B$ with respect to $A$ and velocity of ground with respect to $B$ are (in $ms^{- 1}$):

questions.solution:
${V}_{A} = 72kmh^{- 1} = 72 \times \dfrac{1000}{3600} = 20ms^{- 1}$ and

${V}_{B} = - 108kmh^{- 1} = - 108 \times \dfrac{1000}{3600} = - 30ms^{- 1}$

Velocity of $B$ w.r.t. $A$:

${V}_{B / A} = - 30 - 20 = – 50ms^{- 1}$

Velocity of ground w.r.t. $B$:

${V}_{G / B} = 0 - \left(- 30\right) = 30ms^{- 1}$

questions.q:

(A) The average velocity during 0 to 3 s is $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(B) The average velocity during 3 to 5 s is $0 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(C) The instantaneous velocity at $\mathrm{t}=2 \mathrm{~s}$ is $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(D) The average velocity during 5 to 7 s and instantaneous velocity at $\mathrm{t}=6.5 \mathrm{~s}$ are equal
(E) The average velocity from $t=0$ to $t=9 \mathrm{~s}$ is zero
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \langle\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}\rangle=\frac{\Delta \overrightarrow{\mathrm{s}}}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\frac{\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{i}}} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{\mathrm{ds}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\text { slope }
\end{aligned}$
(A) 0 to $3 \mathrm\sec ;\langle\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}\rangle=\frac{5-0}{3}=5 / 3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(B) 0 to $5 \mathrm\sec ;\langle\vec{v}\rangle=\frac{5-5}{2}=0$
(C) $\mathrm{t}=2 ;$ slope $=\vec{v}=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(D) $\mathfrak{t}=5$ to $7 \mathrm\sec ;\langle\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}\rangle=\frac{0-5}{2}=-2.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
At $t=6.5 \mathrm\sec ; \vec{v}=10$
(E) $\mathrm{t}=0$ to $\mathrm{t}=9 ;\langle\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}\rangle=0$

questions.q: A train starting from rest first accelerates uniformly up to a speed of $80 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ for time $t$, then it moves with a constant speed for time $3 t$. The average speed of the train for this duration of journey will be (in $\mathrm{km} / \mathrm{h}$ ) :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \text { Average speed } & =\frac{\text { total distance }}{\text { time taken }} \\ & =\frac{\frac{80 \times \mathrm{t}}{2}+80 \times 3 \mathrm{t}}{4 \mathrm{t}}=70 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr} .\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The distance travelled by a particle is related to time $t$~as $x = 4t^{2}$. The velocity of the particle at $t = 5s$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $x = 4t^{2}$

We know that velocity is the rate at which displacement changes with time. So,~$v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{d \left(4t^{2}\right)}{d t} = 8t$

Now, at~$t = 5s$

Velocity of particle is~$v = 8 \times 5 = 40ms^{- 1}$.

questions.q: An elevator in a building can carry a maximum of $10$ persons, with the average mass of each person being $68$ kg . The mass of the elevator itself is $920$ kg and it moves with a constant speed of $3m / s$ . The frictional force opposing the motion is $6000N$ . questions.solution:
Net force on motor will be

$= 22000N$
So, required power for motor
${P}_{m} = {\overset{→}{F}}_{m} . \overset{→}{v}$
$= 22000 \times 3$
$= 66000watt$

questions.q: A passenger sitting in a train A moving at $90kmh^{- 1}$ observes another train B moving in the opposite direction for $8s$. If the velocity of the train B is $54kmh^{- 1}$, then length of train B is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the velocity of A be& ${v}_{A}$~and the velocity of B be~${v}_{B}$.

The relative velocity is

$\overset{→}{v}BA = \overset{→}{v}B - \overset{→}{v}A ⇒ {v}_{BA} = 54 - ( - 90 ) = 144kmh^{- 1}$

$⇒ {v}_{BA} = 40ms^{- 1}$

$Time = \dfrac{length}{vBA}$~

$⇒ length = 40ms^{- 1} \times 8s = 320m$

questions.q: A juggler throws balls vertically upwards with same initial velocity in air. When the first ball reaches its highest position, he throws the next ball. Assuming the juggler throws $n$ balls per second, the maximum height the balls can reach is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As the juggler is throwing $n$ balls each second and ${2}^{nd}$ when the first is at its highest point, so the time taken by one ball to reach the highest point,~$t = \dfrac{1}{n}s$.

And as at highest point $v = 0$.

So, from first~equation of motion,

$v = u + at ⇒ 0 = u - g\left(\dfrac{1}{n}\right) ⇒ u = \dfrac{g}{n}$

Now in order to calculate height, using second equation of motion, we have:
$\text{S} = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}{at}^{2}$ ...(i)

$⇒ h = \dfrac{1}{n} \times \dfrac{g}{n} - \dfrac{1}{2}\text{g} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{n}\right)2$

~ ~ ~$⇒ h = \dfrac{g}{2n^{2}}$

So, the balls rise up to a height of~$h = \dfrac{g}{2n^{2}}m$.

options: the acceleration of the particle is $2 \mathrm{c}_0$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \mathrm{tC}_0+2 \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{t}-2) \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \mathrm{C}_0+2 \mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The relation between time ‘$t$’ and distance ‘$x$’ is $t = \alphax^{2} + \betax$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constants. The relation between acceleration  \left(a\right)$ and velocity  \left(v\right)$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: $t = \alphax^{2} + \betax$

Differentiating w.r.t time, we get

$\dfrac{dt}{dx} = 2\alphax + \beta$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{v} = 2\alphax + \beta$

Differentiating w.r.t time again, we get

$⇒ - \dfrac{1}{v2}\dfrac{dv}{dt} = 2\alpha\dfrac{dx}{dt}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dv}{dt} = - 2\alphav^{3}\left[\text{as}v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}\right] ⇒ a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = - 2\alphav^{3}$

questions.q: A person travels $x$ distance with velocity ${v}_{1}$ and then $x$ distance with velocity ${v}_{2}$ in the same direction. The average velocity of the person is $v$, then the relation between $v, {v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The time& \left({t}_{1}\right)$~taken by the person to travel distance~$x$~with velocity~${v}_{1}$~is given by

${t}_{1} = \dfrac{x}{v1} . . . \left(1\right)$

The time~ \left({t}_{2}\right)$~taken by the person to travel distance~$x$~with velocity~${v}_{2}$~is given by

${t}_{2} = $\dfrac{x}{v2} . . . \left(2\right)$

The formula to calculate the average speed~ \left(v\right)$~of the person is given by

$v = $\dfrac{2x}{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2}} . . . \left(3\right)$

Substitute the expressions from equations (1) and (2) into equation (3) to obtain the required relation.

$\begin{cases}v \text{ and } = \text{ and } $2x $\$left(\dfrac{x}{v1} + \dfrac{x}{v2}\right)\\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } \dfrac{x}{v1} + \dfrac{x}{v2} = \dfrac{2x}{v}\\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } \dfrac{2}{v} = \dfrac{1}{v1} + \dfrac{1}{v2}\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: The velocity& $( v )$~and time $( t )$ graph of a body in a straight line motion is shown in the figure. The point $S$ is at $4 . 333$ seconds. The total distance covered by the body in $6s$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Total distance covered by the body is equal to the modulus of area under graph& velocity-time graph

$⇒ d = \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 2\right) + \left(4 \times 1\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times$4 $\times \dfrac{4}{3}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times$2 $\times \dfrac{5}{3}\right)

$⇒ d = 4 + 4 + $\dfrac{8}{3} + \dfrac{5}{3}

$⇒ d = $\dfrac{37}{3}$m$

$

questions.q: A boy pushes a box of mass $2$ kg with a force $\overset{→}{F} = \left(20\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j}\right)N$ on a frictionless surface. If the box was initially at rest, then _______ $m$ is displacement along the $x$-axis after $10s$

questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{F} = 20\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{F}m = \dfrac{20\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j}}{2} ⇒ 10\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j}$

$∴ \overset{→}{s} = \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{→}{a}t^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(10\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j}\right) \times \left(10\right)2$

$⇒ 50\left(10\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j}\right)m$

$∴$ Displacement along $x$-axis

$⇒ 50 \times 10 ⇒ 500m$

questions.q: From the top of a tower, a ball is thrown vertically upward which reaches the ground in $6s$. A second ball thrown vertically downward from the same position with the same speed reaches the ground in $1 . 5s$. A third ball released, from the rest from the same location, will reach the ground in _____ s.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When it is thrown upward,& $- h = v \times 6 - \dfrac{1}{2}g\left(6\right)2$

When it is thrown downward,~$- h = - v \times 1 . 5 - \dfrac{1}{2}g \left(1 . 5\right)2$

Therefore,~$5h = 5\left[36 + 9\right]$~$h = 45m$

When the ball is dropped,~$h = $\dfrac{1}{2}$gt^{2} ⇒ 45 = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times$10 \timest^{2} ⇒ t = 3s$

Alternate method,~$t = $\sqrt{{t}_{1}{t}_{2}} = \sqrt{6 \times 1 . 5} =$3s

$

questions.q: The distance $x$ covered by a paritcle in one dimensional motion varies with time $t$ as $x^{2} = at^{2} + 2bt + c$ . If the acceleration of the particle depends on $x$ as $x^{- n}$ , where $n$ is an integer, the value of $n$ is _________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$x^{2} = at^{2} + 2bt + c$
$2xv = 2at + 2b$
$xv = at + b$
$v^{2} + ax = a$
$ax = a - {\left(\dfrac{at + b}{x}\right)}^{2}$
$a = \dfrac{a\left(at^{2} + 2bt + c\right) - {\left(at + b\right)}^{2}}{x^{3}}$
$a = \dfrac{ac^{- 2}}{x3}$
$a\alphax^{- 3}$

questions.q: A person travelling on a straight line moves with a uniform velocity $\mathrm{v}_1$ for a distance x and with a uniform velocity $\mathrm{v}_2$ for the next $\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{x}$ distance. The average velocity in this motion is $\frac{50}{7} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If $\mathrm{v}_1$ is $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ then $\mathrm{v}_2=$ _________ $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{v}_{\text {avg }}=\frac{\mathrm{x}_1+\mathrm{x}_2}{\mathrm{t}_1+\mathrm{t}_2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{50}{7}=\frac{\mathrm{x}+\frac{3 \mathrm{x}}{2}}{\frac{\mathrm{x}}{5}+\frac{3 \mathrm{x}}{2 \mathrm{v}_2}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{50}{7}=\frac{5 / 2}{\frac{1}{5}+\frac{3}{2 \mathrm{v}_2}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{5}+\frac{3}{2 \mathrm{v}_2}=\frac{7}{20}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2 \mathrm{v}_2}=\frac{7}{20}-\frac{1}{5}=\frac{7-4}{20} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2 \mathrm{v}_2}=\frac{3}{20} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}_2=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle is moving with constant acceleration $a .$ Following graph shows $v^{2}$ versus~$x$~(displacement) plot. The acceleration of the particle is _________~$ms^{- 2} .$

questions.solution:
The equation of the straight& line,& $y = mx + c$, from the above graph we get the equation,~$v^{2} = 2x + 20$, now differentiate it with respect to~$x$,~
$⇒ 2v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 2 ⇒ a = \dfrac{2}{2} = 1ms^{- 2}$.
